title: Improve tensor-parallel NCCL tuning and overlap comm/compute for multi-GPU runtime
author: Asha Patel
commits: opt: tune NCCL algorithm selection heuristics for reduce-scatter/all-reduce based on tensor shape/size
perf: overlap NCCL comm with attention-key/value compute and KV cache ops in TP codepath
kernels: add fast-path for fused rotary+qkv reorder for TP shards
scheduler: introduce op-level dependency barriers to enable safe compute/comm overlap
tests: add multi-gpu integration perf canary and TP microbench harness
docs: update runtime/README with TP tuning knobs and rollout guidance
description:
Motivation: Multi-GPU tensor-parallel workloads were seeing suboptimal throughput in medium-sequence (1k-2k) regimes due to conservative NCCL algorithm selection and serialized comm/compute phases. This PR improves end-to-end throughput and tail latency by exposing heuristics for NCCL collective selection, introducing a light-weight scheduler to safely overlap NCCL comms with attention KV compute, and adding a few kernel-level fast-paths for common QKV reorder patterns.

Summary of changes: - NCCL tuner: added heuristics that choose reduce-scatter/all-reduce algorithms (ring vs tree vs tree+ring hybrid) based on per-tensor size, peer count and device topology. The tuner also probes small windows at runtime to adjust for contention. - Comm-overlap scheduler: new op-level dependency tracking to allow KV generation and local attention compute to proceed while NCCL transfers are in-flight, avoiding hazards via explicit barriers. - KV cache: improved shard manager to prefetch/flush KV pages aligned with overlapped transfers and to expose metrics for hot-key detection. - Kernels: fused rotary + qkv reorder kernel for TP shards to reduce memory traffic and free compute to overlap with communication. - Tests & benchmarks: added perf canary and integration test that measures steady-state tokens/s, p50/p95 latency and NCCL bandwidth utilization. - Docs: added tuning guide and rollout checklist.

Benchmarks: On internal canary runs (8xA100, fp16, sequence 1024, batch size tuned for target latency) we observe: - Tokens/sec: +21% steady-state throughput on GPT-like 13B model with TP=4 and DP=2. - Average per-token latency: -12% in steady-state synthetic workload. - p95 token latency: -18% when overlapped successfully; worst-case regressions in microbench with heavy host contention were mitigated by the tuner fallback. - NCCL bandwidth utilization improved by ~15% on multi-node runs after algorithm tuning.

Compatibility and safety: All changes are gated behind a runtime flag tp.enable_nccl_tuner and tp.enable_comm_overlap (both default off). The NCCL tuner has a conservative probe and a safe rollback path to previous algorithm selection. The scheduler ensures dependency correctness via explicit barriers; any layout that cannot be safely overlapped will fall back to conservative ordering.

Testing: - Unit tests for tuner heuristics and fallback logic. - Integration perf canary added under perf/canaries. - Multi-node CI run in internal perf lab validated the stability over 4k token streams for 1 hour. - Nightly regression benchmarks added.

Rollout plan: 1) Enable flags in dedicated perf clusters and run extended canaries. 2) Gradual rollout to a subset of hosted clusters with traffic shaping. 3) Monitor metrics (tokens/s, p95 latency, NCCL errors, GPU SM utilization). 4) If any NCCL errors or unexpected tail regressions appear, toggle tp.enable_comm_overlap=false and let tuner remain on for algorithm improvements.

Related work: PRs pr-18742 and pr-19105 provided baseline NCCL collective overlap experiments; this PR builds on that by adding production-safe heuristics, scheduler primitives, and kernel fast-paths.

Checklist: - [x] Add unit and integration tests - [x] Perf canary results attached - [x] Docs and tuning guide included - [x] Feature flags for safe rollout

Notes: This change targets serving runtime perf improvements and should be reviewed by runtime and infra owners. See docs/runtime/tp_tuning.md for operator guidance and perf figures.
review_comments: Ethan Zhao: Nice work. Can you quantify when the tuner decides to switch algorithms? I worry about oscillation under load.

Asha Patel: The tuner uses a hysteresis window and requires improvement above 7% steady throughput for two consecutive probe windows before committing. I've added tests to validate no flip-flop under synthetic variable load.
Carlos Ruiz: Scheduler looks good, but we should ensure no extra CPU overhead from dependency tracking on hot paths.
Asha Patel: dependency tracking is implemented with lock-free counters per op and the hot path remains inlined; added microbench showing <1% CPU overhead on our perf harness.
Maya Singh: Approving pending green CI and perf canary stability on dedicated cluster.
